question.problem: What is the coefficient of $(x+2)^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x)$ at $x=-2?$
question.worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=-2$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2))(x+2)+\frac{{f}^{″}(-2)}{2}(x+2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is 

$$
\frac{{f}^{″}(-2)}{2}.
$$

$$

$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x) \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{1}{1-x} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{1}{(1-x)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=-2.$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(-2)=-\frac{1}{(1-(-2))^{2}}=-\frac{1}{9}.
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x+2)^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(-2)}{2} & =\frac{(-\frac{1}{9})}{2}=-\frac{1}{18}\end{aligned}
$$
